solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film Isaac's wife

definitions.meaning: the 1940 Hitchcock thriller named after the unseen first Mrs de Winter
in Genesis, the woman Abraham's servant found as a bride for Isaac

explanation.definitionFit: The name serves both as a Hitchcock film title and as the biblical matriarch married to Isaac.

clue.text: Go over about fuel

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
peat is dug and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: Discussing the fuel question again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go over something is to repeat it, as in revising.

clue.text: Good man invested in good thing in US city

indicators.note: the good man is placed inside the good thing, like money invested in it

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
ST, for saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous person putting money into a worthwhile American project.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts, a major city in the USA.

clue.text: CO at a drugs bust?

indicators.note: a bust breaks things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A commanding officer present at a drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' is both the police raid and the anagram signal; a coastguard officer might well be at a seizure of smuggled drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastguards patrol coasts and intercept smugglers, so one could be the officer at a drugs raid.

clue.text: Adult with energy, energy in abundance

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'
go again, as energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A grown-up bursting with vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo, from French, means in plenty or galore, as in 'wine a gogo'.

clue.text: Representative put in new suite, as an incentive

indicators.note: the representative is placed inside the reworked letters of the other word
something new is made afresh, so the letters of suite are rearranged

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A politician moving into a fresh hotel suite as a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the five letters of the furnishing word and 'put in' lodges the politician among them; 'as an' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an impetus is a driving force or stimulus that spurs someone to act.

clue.text: I wish rest could make a nourishing dish

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be arranged to make something else

explanation.surface: Someone wishing for a rest from cooking a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a hearty dish of mutton, potatoes and onions.

clue.text: Friend carrying one's bucket

indicators.note: the friend holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A friend carrying someone's bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pail is a bucket.

clue.text: Playwright with point to get across

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of 1920s London
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A dramatist trying to get a point across.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to traverse something is to cross it from side to side.

clue.text: Copy detailed working description, mine smudged

parts.note: a spec, short for specification, describes how something works in detail

indicators.note: smudged letters are blurred out of order, so mine is rearranged

explanation.surface: A copy of a technical document of mine gets smudged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy' sounds like a verb but is the noun: a sample or example; 'smudged' scrambles only the four letters of the possessive word.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or example, a representative copy of something.

clue.text: Finished last of pizza, Italian food

parts.note: something finished is over and done, past

indicators.note: only the final letter of pizza is taken

explanation.surface: Someone eating up the final slice of a pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a staple dish of Italian cooking, made from durum wheat dough.

clue.text: Start to make a speech about one mother's ruin

indicators.note: the speech-making word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a formal speech
the Roman numeral for one is I
a traditional British nickname for gin, the cheap spirit blamed for ruining families in the 1700s

explanation.surface: Someone beginning a lecture on the evils of gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to originate something is to start or initiate it.

clue.text: A character in 'Howard's End'

parts.note: seems to ask for a person in the E. M. Forster novel, but means a typographical mark found in the title as printed

explanation.walkthrough: The novel is properly 'Howards End' without punctuation; the clue's version contains a mark between D and S, and that mark is the 'character'.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing possession is a typographic character, and one sits in the misprinted title.

clue.text: I was first to go round shop

indicators.note: the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: someone who led was at the front, first

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of being the first person to walk round a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns I + LED into the four-letter shop; 'to go' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Hurt in boisterous performance

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both beating someone up and a slapstick act full of rough horseplay.

clue.text: Q. Will I like this lollipop? A. — — — –!

definitions.text: Q. Will I like this lollipop? A. — — — –!

parts.words: Q. Will I like this lollipop? A. — — — –!
parts.note: a child's question about a sweet, answered by an idiom for trying something to find out, literally fitting a lollipop

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means 'try it and find out', and here a lollipop makes the words literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiomatic reply to an uncertain question is to try the thing and discover the result yourself.

clue.text: Relative knows man I ruined

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative who knows the man the speaker has ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinswoman is a female relative.

clue.text: Topliner abroad in crime unit

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of the word are dispersed

explanation.surface: A star performer overseas embroiled in an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation coordinating action against crime.

clue.text: In which one may see Odette boast about the French leading English

definitions.text: In which one may see Odette

indicators.note: the first part comes ahead of the English abbreviation
the boasting word goes around the French article

parts.note: to swank is to show off or boast
la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone bragging that French dancers lead the English ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Odette is the swan princess in Tchaikovsky's ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is the heroine of that Tchaikovsky ballet, so she is seen in it.

clue.text: Young bishop manages town in Scotland or province in Canada

parts.note: something young is new
B is the chess notation for bishop
to run a business is to manage it
Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A new bishop takes charge of a parish in Scotland or abroad in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: New Brunswick is one of Canada's Maritime provinces, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Petty quarrel at home making lunch for expat

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble
in means at home

explanation.surface: A domestic squabble over a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light midday meal, the word used by the British in colonial India.

clue.text: Plot to strike causes uproar

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot for flowers
to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to stage a strike causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a scheme, but it is a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from London's old Bethlem asylum, means chaotic uproar.

clue.text: Eagle from Els knocking one out

indicators.note: one, the numeral I, is removed from the golfer's first name

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer scoring an eagle on a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an eagle is two under par, which makes the surface feel at home on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: Son, waist-deep, in trouble, is ignored

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disordered, so waist-deep is rearranged

explanation.surface: A son stuck waist-deep in water is overlooked by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles the whole hyphenated word; 'is' is a link, since the definition must be a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something swept aside has been dismissed or disregarded.

clue.text: Old man overlooking insect turning up in rice

indicators.note: in a down clue, the father sits above the following piece

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: in a down clue, the insect reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Father watching an insect crawl up through his rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Patna is a long-grain rice named after the city in India.

clue.text: Star in another opera

indicators.note: the word lies inside the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A singer starring in another opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hero is the star or principal figure of a story.

clue.text: Rug a martyr used round the East after start of pilgrimage

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay follows the opening letter
only the first letter of pilgrimage is taken
the rearranged letters go around the compass point
letters used are worked over, so a martyr is rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A martyr kneeling on a rug facing east at the start of a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges A MARTYR as RAYRMAT, and 'round' puts E inside it after RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer mat is a small rug on which Muslims kneel for prayer.

clue.text: Waste away by a lake

parts.note: off means away, as in 'off on holiday'
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone wasting away beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste away' looks like a verb phrase, but 'Waste' alone is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and trimmings of a butchered animal, often thought of as waste.

clue.text: Rest have told untruths before

indicators.note: the lying piece comes ahead of the possessing piece

parts.note: someone who told untruths lied
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Liars told to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to lie down is to rest horizontally.

clue.text: An American theatre award presented to male? The opposite

parts.note: the Tony is the Broadway theatre award

explanation.surface: A Tony award being handed to a man, followed by a question about its contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, so it is literally an opposite.
